response.question: I am finishing my home office. Check the Dell U2720Q (B0939N79Y8) for a 27-inch 4K screen and USB-C charging up to 90W, and the Steelcase Gesture (B01NAKXH73) for adjustable lumbar support and movable arms. Search each product separately, compare their fit for these needs, and explain what the specifications and available reviews do and do not establish. Cite the supporting records and explain the ranking of one search.
response.answer:
### What the sources support

The Dell UltraSharp 27" 4K UHD... U2720Q-Black listing confirms a 27-inch screen at 3840 x 2160 resolution and USB-C power delivery up to 90W, matching the display and charging requirements [1]. The Steelcase Gesture Task Chair... Adjustable Lumbar Support listing confirms adjustable lumbar support and arms designed to move like a human arm, matching the ergonomic requirement [2]. Both records are catalog product specifications, not customer reviews; no review excerpts were supplied for either product, so no source here speaks to comfort over time, screen color accuracy in use, or chair durability.

### What remains uncertain

Because no reviews were retrieved, real-world experience with either product is unestablished [1][2]. For the monitor search, the top-ranked result reflects full-text, trigram, and semantic signals fused and then reranked to a high but non-probabilistic reranker score, not an exact SKU match [1].

Description:
The first chair designed to support our interactions with today’s technologies. It was inspired by the movement of the human body and created for the way we work today. To address this new workplace landscape, Steelcase photographed 2000 people in 11 countries to study their posture. The culmination of these new finding resulted in the Gesture Chair, inspired by the everyday movement of the human body. Like the human body, Gesture is designed as a system of synchronized interfaces that together provide customized support for any posture.
Features:
A new sitting experience designed with a back and seat that move as a synchronized system moving with each user to provide continuous and persistent support
Arms move like a human arm which allows users to be supported in any position
Seat has comfort all the way to the edge with a flexible perimeter to allow users to sit in a range of positions
Arms and shoulders remain supported regardless of device being used
Designed to be quickly adjustable and takes into account various body types and sitting preferences

Categories: Office Products > Office Furniture & Lighting > Chairs & Sofas > Managerial & Executive Chairs

Description:
The first chair designed to support our interactions with today’s technologies. It was inspired by the movement of the human body and created for the way we work today. More now than ever, our business is conducted through smartphones, tablets, and laptops. The generational spread of the office is increasing too, with decades of professionals working together. With all this change happening around us, Steelcase set out to create a chair that reflects the way we work and live. To address this new workplace landscape, Steelcase photographed 2000 people in 11 countries to study their posture. The culmination of these new finding resulted in the Gesture Chair, inspired by the everyday movement of the human body. Like the human body, Gesture is designed as a system of synchronized interfaces that together provide customized support for any posture.
Features:
A new sitting experience designed with a back and seat that move as a synchronized system moving with each user to provide continuous and persistent support
Arms move like a human arm which allows users to be supported in any position
Seat has comfort all the way to the edge with a flexible perimeter to allow users to sit in a range of positions
Arms and shoulders remain supported regardless of device being used
Designed to be quickly adjustable and takes into account various body types and sitting preferences
